title: The regular who isn't
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Tuesday, week four. A second regular. A woman in waders who takes the stool next to Wood's and says nothing for the whole strip. The strip draws her the way it draws the uncle: as a fact.

panels.composition: The shack. WOOD on the end stool. Beside him, a WOMAN in waders, sixties, coffee, silent. GULLY. BARNABY.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a thin teenager on a shack's end stool and a silent older woman in waders on the next one, both with coffee, a teenager in an apron behind the counter, a dog beneath
image.notes: The woman in waders: reserved who. A fact, not a character.

panels.composition: Her hands around the cup. Rope burns. Rings on the wrong fingers.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, close-up of an older woman's weathered hands around a coffee cup, rope-marked

panels.composition: Wood drawing her. She sees. She doesn't move. She lets him.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a teenager sketching a silent older woman beside him who notices and does not move, no words

panels.composition: She leaves a dollar and goes. Gully, to Wood.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a teenager in an apron speaking to another after a customer has left a dollar and gone

art.line: brush-pen, committed; xerox; black and white

notes: The second regular. 'That's how you can tell.'
